newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling marginally firmer against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling marginally firmer against dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling was marginally firmer against the dollar on Wednesday as heavy exporter sales came into the market, dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling average of 55.74 from 55.75 on Tuesday. Against the pound, the shilling was posted at 89.79 from 89.77 on Tuesday.
"The dollar received some pounding as heavy exporter sales rocked the market, with an offshore bank selling about $6 million to the market," a commercial dealer said.
"The market opened at 55.73/83 and slid down to trade at 55.66/76 level as coffee dealers came in to offload $1.5 million," another dealer added.
Dealers said continued depreciation of the dollar was halted as many importers came in to cover their month end commitments.
The central bank adopted a 'wait-and-see' attitude, refusing to come in and mop up excess dollars in the market, they said.
Dealers said that the money market was a bit tight with funds already tied in the repurchase agreement market. Rates went up to 20 percent from 15 percent on Tuesday, they added.
